newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel seals West Bank, Gaza after bloody clashes.
newsitem.headline: Israel seals West Bank, Gaza after bloody clashes.

text.p: Security forces sealed off the West Bank and the Gaza Strip on Thursday, fearing a recurrence of violent clashes in which Israeli troops killed seven Palestinians and wounded hundreds on Wednesday, the army said.

"In a special assessment of the defence minister and other authorities it has been decided to impose a full closure on Judea and Samaria (the West Bank) and Gaza to allow a calming of passions and to prevent new flareups like the one on Wednesday," an army spokeswoman said. "The closure is already in effect."

Israeli soldiers shot dead seven Palestinians, at least three of them police, in gun battles and clashes with stone-throwers on the edge of the PLO-ruled enclave of Ramallah, north of Jerusalem on Wednesday. Doctors said more than 300 were injured, several critically.

Fierce clashes also erupted in Bethlehem, plunging relations between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu into crisis and unnerving the United States, sponsor of Middle East peacemaking.

Rival Palestinian factions issued a joint statement on Wednesday calling for a Palestinian day of mourning and two-hour strikes across the West Bank and Gaza on Thursday. The unrest was sparked by Israel's opening of a tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem near Islam's third-holiest site.

Israel has maintained a partial closure on the West Bank and Gaza since a wave of Islamic suicide bombings that killed 59 people in the Jewish state began in late February. But the prolonged closure, which has crippled the Palestinian economy by keeping thousands of workers from jobs in Israel, has been relaxed somewhat in the interim.
